title: Development and validation of a novel interpretable machine learning model integrating immune-inflammatory indicators for intravenous immunoglobulin resistance in Kawasaki disease.
summary: Interpretable models using immune-inflammatory indicators predicted IVIG resistance in Kawasaki disease and were evaluated in development/validation cohorts; the retrospective prediction result does not establish treatment benefit.
ai_technology: LightGBM, random forest, XGBoost, neural network, SVM and ElasticNet logistic regression models predict IVIG resistance in children with Kawasaki disease; SHAP explains feature contributions.

evidence.tested: Among 1,584 patients, LightGBM achieved test-set AUC 0.832 (95% CI 0.766–0.898), sensitivity 0.860 and specificity 0.639; leading features included fever duration, NLR, IL-1β, albumin and AST.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective single-hospital data were randomly divided into training and test sets; external prospective performance is unknown.
evidence.ai_role: LightGBM, random forest, XGBoost, neural network, SVM and ElasticNet logistic regression models predict IVIG resistance in children with Kawasaki disease; SHAP explains feature contributions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
